sb_prompt: DISCUSS THE CHANGES IN THE ROLES OF WOMEN IN AMERICAN SOCIETY OVER THE PAST GENERATION OR TWO.  WHICH CHANGES HAVE BEEN THE MOST SIGNIFICANT? DO YOU HAVE AN OPINION ON WHAT FURTHER CHANGES WILL TAKE PLACE OVER THE NEXT GENERATION?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Hi, can I ask you a favor? My name is Sarah, by the way.
ParticipantB: Sure, sure. I'm Mark.
ParticipantA: Thanks, Mark. So, I was thinking, do you have a few minutes to chat about women's roles in society?
ParticipantB: Yeah, sure. I mean, that's a big topic.
ParticipantA: It is, it is. You know, looking back, it's wild to see how much things have changed in my lifetime.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I guess. I just don't really see it as much in my own job, but I get it.
ParticipantA: That's interesting. What about your job? Do you see women in your field?
ParticipantB: Oh, yeah. We got a new mechanic in last month. She's been there six months.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? That's great. Does she do everything?
ParticipantB: Yeah, pretty much. She's good. But, uh, she's got to take a lot of extra time to explain stuff to the customers sometimes.
ParticipantA: Oh, really? That's a shame. I've known this one lady at the bank, she's retired now, but she used to be a teller for twenty years.
ParticipantB: Oh? How was it for her?
ParticipantA: It was really tough for her. She'd have to hide her hands behind the counter sometimes because the guys kept staring.
ParticipantB: Staring? That's bad.
ParticipantA: Yeah, yeah. And she'd get yelled at if she made a mistake, even if it wasn't her fault. Her boss just said, "Can't a woman get a break?"
ParticipantB: Wow. That sounds rough.
ParticipantA: It really was. But now, my niece is studying to be an engineer. She's smart, really smart.
ParticipantB: Oh, that's cool.
ParticipantA: Yeah. And she says she's not gonna have that problem. She says people are finally paying attention to what you can do, not just what you are.
ParticipantB: I guess so. I mean, I don't know about that part. I've been a mechanic for ten years, mostly just guys.
ParticipantA: Really? No women at all?
ParticipantB: Well, there was this one girl, maybe two years ago. She was nice, but she just seemed confused. Like, she didn't know how to use the tools right.
ParticipantA: Maybe she needed training?
ParticipantB: Maybe. But honestly, she just quit after a month. Said she couldn't handle the pressure.
ParticipantA: That's too bad. I can't imagine giving up on that.
ParticipantB: Well, I guess everyone has limits. I mean, being a mechanic is tough. It's dirty, loud, high stress. Maybe it's just not for everyone.
ParticipantA: Oh, I see. But my niece says women are actually better at diagnosing problems sometimes.
ParticipantB: Hmm. Maybe. I never noticed that before.
ParticipantA: Really? Why not?
ParticipantB: I don't know. I just didn't think about it. I've just been used to guys in the shop.
ParticipantA: That's what I mean. It's the mindset, I think. We need to stop assuming women can't do the job.
ParticipantB: Yeah, maybe. I mean, I don't know if it's gonna change much more. Things seem pretty set in my line of work.
ParticipantA: Maybe for mechanics. But I think for things like leadership, or science, or politics, it's still shifting.
ParticipantB: Oh? What do you mean?
ParticipantA: Well, look at the news. Women are getting elected everywhere now. It's just a generation ago that it was unthinkable.
ParticipantB: True. That is a big change. I didn't think that would happen in my lifetime.
ParticipantA: It's amazing. I'm so happy for it. What do you think will happen in the next generation?
ParticipantB: I don't know. Maybe more women in my shop?
ParticipantA: That would be great.
ParticipantB: Yeah. Maybe. Or maybe just people who don't care who's fixing the car.
ParticipantA: Exactly! That's what I hope for. Just competence, regardless of gender.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that would be nice. No more "you can't do that."
ParticipantA: Right. And maybe men will admit when they're bad at something, too.
ParticipantB: Ha! Yeah, that might happen.
ParticipantA: Anyway, I've gotta run. My shift is almost over.
ParticipantB: Okay, well, take care.
ParticipantA: You too, Mark. Thanks for talking.
ParticipantB: Sure thing. Bye.
